channel.title: Sahaj's blog
channel.description: Study notes, AI updates and paper summaries by Sahaj Saliya.

item.title: Paper summary: DataFlow: An LLM-Driven Framework for Unified Data Preparation and Workflow Automation in the Era of Data-Centric AI
item.description: DataFlow is an LLM-driven framework for building data-preparation pipelines from about 200 reusable operators with a PyTorch-style API, plus an agent that turns plain-language specs into pipelines.

item.title: Transformers · Hugging Face Transformers: fine-tuning
item.description: Fine-tuning a small pretrained encoder (BERT-mini) for sentiment on Rotten Tomatoes with a plain PyTorch loop, and an honest comparison with the TF-IDF baseline from my NLP phase.

item.title: Paper summary: Kling-Omni Technical Report
item.description: Kling-Omni is one end-to-end framework for video generation, editing and reasoning-based editing from mixed inputs (text, reference images, video context), built on a dedicated data system.

item.title: Transformers · Hugging Face Transformers: pipelines
item.description: The pipeline() API for quick inference (sentiment, zero-shot classification, NER, summarisation) and what happens inside: tokenizer → model → post-processing.

item.title: Paper summary: Wan-Move: Motion-controllable Video Generation via Latent Trajectory Guidance
item.description: Wan-Move adds precise motion control to an image-to-video model by turning dense point trajectories into a motion-aware latent condition, with no architecture change; user studies rate it close to Kling 1.5 Pro's Motion Brush.

item.title: Transformers · Vision Transformer (ViT)
item.description: ViT treats an image as a sequence of 16×16 patches with a [CLS] token and position embeddings; patch arithmetic, and a pretrained ViT classifying a photo.

item.title: Paper summary: From Code Foundation Models to Agents and Applications: A Comprehensive Survey and Practical Guide to Code Intelligence
item.description: A large survey and practical guide to code LLMs, from data curation and pre-training through SFT, RL and coding agents, comparing general and code-specialised models and the gap between benchmarks and real development.

item.title: Paper summary: General Agentic Memory Via Deep Research
item.description: General Agentic Memory keeps a light memory plus the full history in a page-store, then uses a "researcher" agent to build the right context at request time, like just-in-time compilation for memory.

item.title: Transformers · GPT
item.description: GPT as a decoder-only Transformer trained to predict the next token; generating with GPT-2, measuring perplexity, and seeing why causal masking makes this possible.

item.title: Paper summary: Kandinsky 5.0: A Family of Foundation Models for Image and Video Generation
item.description: Kandinsky 5.0 is an open family of image and 10-second video generation models (6B Image Lite, 2B Video Lite, 19B Video Pro), with the full data-curation and multi-stage training pipeline described.

item.title: Transformers · BERT
item.description: BERT as a bidirectional encoder pretrained with masked language modelling; running fill-mask, looking at [CLS] and [SEP], and seeing contextual embeddings change with meaning.

item.title: Paper summary: Lumine: An Open Recipe for Building Generalist Agents in 3D Open Worlds
item.description: Lumine is an open recipe for a generalist game-playing agent built on a vision-language model: pixels in at 5 Hz, keyboard and mouse out at 30 Hz, completing a five-hour storyline and transferring zero-shot to other games.

item.title: Paper summary: Thinking with Video: Video Generation as a Promising Multimodal Reasoning Paradigm
item.description: "Thinking with Video" uses a video generation model (Sora-2) as a reasoner, drawing its solution as video frames; on a new benchmark it rivals strong VLMs on visual puzzles and reaches 92% on MATH.

item.title: Transformers · Encoder and decoder
item.description: How the encoder layer, the decoder layer and cross-attention fit together, with residual connections and layer norm, and the three families they led to: encoder-only, decoder-only and encoder–decoder.

item.title: Paper summary: Scaling Latent Reasoning via Looped Language Models
item.description: Ouro builds latent reasoning into pre-training with looped language models (iterating in latent space with a learned depth), and its 1.4B and 2.6B models are reported to match up to 12B models.

item.title: Transformers · Positional encoding
item.description: Why attention needs position information, the sinusoidal encoding from the original paper, learned position embeddings, and the relative-position idea behind RoPE.

item.title: Paper summary: A Theoretical Study on Bridging Internal Probability and Self-Consistency for LLM Reasoning
item.description: A theoretical framework for sampling-based test-time scaling shows self-consistency has high estimation error and perplexity has high modelling error; the hybrid RPC method matches self-consistency with half the samples.

item.title: Transformers · Multi-head attention
item.description: Splitting d_model into several heads so attention can look at different things at once, implemented by reshaping, and checked against nn.MultiheadAttention.

item.title: Paper summary: QeRL: Beyond Efficiency -- Quantization-enhanced Reinforcement Learning for LLMs
item.description: QeRL combines NVFP4 quantisation with LoRA for RL training of LLMs; beyond saving memory and speeding up rollouts, quantisation noise raises policy entropy and helps exploration. It enables RL on a 32B model with one H100.

item.title: Transformers · Self-attention
item.description: Scaled dot-product self-attention from scratch: queries, keys, values, the √d scaling, softmax weights, and a causal mask, checked against PyTorch's built-in function.

item.title: Paper summary: Less is More: Recursive Reasoning with Tiny Networks
item.description: Tiny Recursive Model, a single 2-layer network with 7M parameters that repeatedly refines its answer, reports 45% on ARC-AGI-1 and 8% on ARC-AGI-2, above many large LLMs on these puzzles.

item.title: Paper summary: The Dragon Hatchling: The Missing Link between the Transformer and Models of the Brain
item.description: The Dragon Hatchling (BDH) is a brain-inspired language-model architecture of locally interacting "neuron particles" with Hebbian working memory, reported to match GPT-2 at the same size and to be more interpretable.

item.title: Transformers · Attention Is All You Need
item.description: Reading the 2017 Transformer paper: dropping recurrence entirely, building everything from attention and feed-forward layers, and why that parallelises so well.

item.title: Built this: SIH-AI-Gyani microplastic detector
item.description: A YOLO11 object detector trained to find and classify six types of microplastic polymers in images, built in a single notebook with Ultralytics.

item.title: Computer Vision · Data augmentation
item.description: Label-preserving random transforms (flips, crops, rotation, colour jitter) with torchvision.transforms.v2, applied consistently to images and boxes.

item.title: Paper summary: Qwen3-Omni Technical Report
item.description: Qwen3-Omni is a single model across text, image, audio and video that's reported to match same-sized single-modal Qwen models, with a Thinker–Talker MoE design and 234 ms theoretical first-packet speech latency.

item.title: Paper summary: FlowRL: Matching Reward Distributions for LLM Reasoning
item.description: FlowRL replaces reward maximisation with matching the whole reward distribution (via a learnable partition function and reverse KL), to keep diverse reasoning paths alive; it reports +10.0% over GRPO on maths.

item.title: Computer Vision · Segmentation and U-Net
item.description: Semantic segmentation as per-pixel classification, the U-Net encoder–decoder with skip connections, Dice/IoU, and a tiny U-Net trained on synthetic shapes.

item.title: Paper summary: Sharing is Caring: Efficient LM Post-Training with Collective RL Experience Sharing
item.description: SAPO is a fully decentralised, asynchronous RL post-training method in which many heterogeneous nodes train their own models but share rollouts, reporting up to 94% higher cumulative reward in controlled tests.

item.title: Computer Vision · Object detection and YOLO
item.description: Detection as boxes plus classes, IoU, non-maximum suppression, YOLO's single-pass grid idea, and running a pretrained torchvision detector on a NASA photo.

item.title: Computer Vision · Transfer learning
item.description: Reusing an ImageNet-pretrained ResNet-18: frozen features plus a new linear head versus training from scratch, on the 8×8 digits upsampled.

item.title: Paper summary: A.S.E: A Repository-Level Benchmark for Evaluating Security in AI-Generated Code
item.description: A.S.E is a repository-level benchmark for the security of AI-generated code; it finds that current LLMs still struggle with secure coding, and that a bigger reasoning budget doesn't reliably help.

item.title: Paper summary: InternVL3.5: Advancing Open-Source Multimodal Models in Versatility, Reasoning, and Efficiency
item.description: InternVL3.5 adds Cascade RL (offline then online RL), a Visual Resolution Router and decoupled vision/language deployment, reporting up to +16% reasoning and 4.05× faster inference than InternVL3.

item.title: Computer Vision · CNN architectures: VGG and ResNet
item.description: VGG's stacks of 3×3 convolutions, why very deep plain networks got worse, and ResNet's skip connections, with a residual block checked in code.

item.title: Paper summary: DINOv3
item.description: DINOv3 scales self-supervised vision training and introduces Gram anchoring to stop dense feature maps from degrading during long training, producing a frozen backbone that beats specialised models across many tasks.

item.title: Computer Vision · CNN architectures: LeNet to AlexNet
item.description: The two early milestones, LeNet-5 for digits and AlexNet for ImageNet: their layers, parameter counts, and what changed between them.

item.title: Paper summary: GLM-4.5: Agentic, Reasoning, and Coding (ARC) Foundation Models
item.description: GLM-4.5 is an open MoE LLM (355B total, 32B active) with hybrid thinking and direct modes, trained on 23T tokens plus expert iteration and RL, reporting 70.1% TAU-Bench, 91.0% AIME 24 and 64.2% SWE-bench Verified.

item.title: Computer Vision · OpenCV essentials
item.description: The OpenCV operations I use most: colour conversion, resizing, Gaussian blur, Canny edges, thresholding and contours.

item.title: Paper summary: Qwen-Image Technical Report
item.description: Qwen-Image is an image-generation foundation model focused on rendering complex text (including Chinese) inside images and on consistent image editing, using a text-rendering curriculum and dual encoding of the input image.

item.title: Computer Vision · Image basics
item.description: Images as arrays: height × width × channels, uint8 vs float, RGB vs grayscale, cropping, and the channel-order and range traps between libraries.

item.title: Paper summary: Agentic Reinforced Policy Optimization
item.description: ARPO is an RL algorithm for multi-turn tool-using agents that samples extra rollouts right after tool calls, where the model's token entropy spikes, and is reported to beat trajectory-level RL with half the tool calls.

item.title: Paper summary: Group Sequence Policy Optimization
item.description: Group Sequence Policy Optimization computes importance ratios and clipping at the level of whole sequences rather than tokens, and is reported to be more stable and efficient than GRPO, especially for MoE models.

item.title: Built this: PyEnv Launcher
item.description: A desktop control centre for Python projects: find and manage venv/Conda environments, packages, Git status and project folders from one window.

item.title: NLP · Text classification
item.description: Multi-class topic classification on 20 Newsgroups, comparing Naive Bayes, logistic regression and a linear SVM, with a per-class report and the most confused pairs.

item.title: Paper summary: A Survey of Context Engineering for Large Language Models
item.description: A survey of over 1,400 papers that defines "context engineering": retrieving, processing and managing everything put into an LLM's context, and how RAG, memory, tools and multi-agent systems build on it.

item.title: NLP · Sentiment analysis
item.description: Classifying movie-review sentiment on the Rotten Tomatoes dataset: a TF-IDF plus logistic regression baseline, its most telling words, and where it fails.

item.title: Paper summary: MemOS: A Memory OS for AI System
item.description: MemOS proposes a memory operating system for LLMs that manages plaintext, activation-based and parameter-level memory as one schedulable resource, built around "MemCube" units with provenance and versioning.

item.title: NLP · Named entity recognition
item.description: NER as token-level sequence labelling with BIO tags, running spaCy's pretrained pipeline, and why entity spans make evaluation tricky.

item.title: Paper summary: GLM-4.5V and GLM-4.1V-Thinking: Towards Versatile Multimodal Reasoning with Scalable Reinforcement Learning
item.description: GLM-4.1V-Thinking and GLM-4.5V use a reasoning-centric training framework with Reinforcement Learning with Curriculum Sampling (RLCS); GLM-4.5V is reported to lead open models of its size on nearly all of 42 benchmarks.

item.title: NLP · Attention (Bahdanau)
item.description: Additive attention lets the decoder look at every encoder state instead of one summary vector; the same reversal task with attention, and its alignment weights.

item.title: Paper summary: Drag-and-Drop LLMs: Zero-Shot Prompt-to-Weights
item.description: Drag-and-Drop LLMs train a generator that maps a few unlabelled task prompts straight to LoRA weights, specialising an LLM for a new task in seconds without any gradient-based fine-tuning on it.

item.title: NLP · Seq2seq
item.description: The encoder–decoder architecture for sequence-to-sequence tasks, teacher forcing, and a small GRU model learning to reverse digit strings.

item.title: Paper summary: MiniMax-M1: Scaling Test-Time Compute Efficiently with Lightning Attention
item.description: MiniMax-M1 is an open-weight hybrid-attention reasoning model (456B total, 45.9B active, 1M-token context) trained with large-scale RL and a new algorithm, CISPO, at a reported rental cost of $534,700.

item.title: Paper summary: Reinforcement Pre-Training
item.description: Reinforcement Pre-Training reframes next-token prediction as a reasoning task: the model reasons before predicting the next token and gets a verifiable reward when it's right, so ordinary text becomes RL training data.

item.title: NLP · GloVe
item.description: GloVe vectors from global co-occurrence statistics, loading pretrained 50-dimensional vectors, analogies, and the bias these vectors inherit.

item.title: Paper summary: Reflect, Retry, Reward: Self-Improving LLMs via Reinforcement Learning
item.description: When a model fails a task, it writes a self-reflection and tries again; if the retry succeeds, the reflection tokens are rewarded, which trains better self-reflection with only binary feedback.

item.title: NLP · word2vec
item.description: Dense word vectors learned by predicting context (skip-gram), trained with gensim on the 20 Newsgroups corpus, with nearest neighbours.

item.title: Paper summary: Mutarjim: Advancing Bidirectional Arabic-English Translation with a Small Language Model
item.description: Mutarjim is a 1.5B-parameter Arabic–English translation model that's reported to rival models up to 20× larger, plus Tarjama-25, a new 5,000-pair benchmark built to fix gaps in existing test sets.

item.title: NLP · Bag of words and TF-IDF
item.description: Turning documents into vectors with CountVectorizer and TfidfVectorizer, n-grams, and finding similar documents with cosine similarity.

item.title: Paper summary: Qwen3 Technical Report
item.description: Qwen3 merges a "thinking" mode for multi-step reasoning and a fast non-thinking mode in one model family (0.6B to 235B, dense and MoE), adds a thinking budget, and expands to 119 languages.
